design_decisions.title: Use ESP32-S3 bare chip for Rev A product path
design_decisions.rationale: The wearable badge form factor needs control over antenna placement, memory selection and board area.
design_decisions.impact: Rev A must include flash, PSRAM, crystal, RF matching and stricter PCB layout review.

design_decisions.title: Use U.FL/IPEX antenna connector for first bare-chip RF bring-up
design_decisions.rationale: An external antenna path reduces RF uncertainty while the audio and power chain are still being validated.
design_decisions.impact: PCB antenna can be added or selected in a later revision after mechanical constraints are better understood.

design_decisions.title: Model the complete Rev A functional chain before locking parts
design_decisions.rationale: USB, power, ESP32-S3 boot, memory, crystal, RF, audio, storage and privacy controls all affect the pin budget and board layout.
design_decisions.impact: Exact LCSC parts remain unresolved until JLC search and footprint download can be verified.

design_decisions.title: Use two I2S MEMS microphones on a shared stereo bus
design_decisions.rationale: A shared I2S bus keeps the Rev A wiring simple while allowing left/right capture and single-mic fallback.
design_decisions.impact: Microphone left/right select polarity must be verified after choosing the exact microphone.

design_decisions.title: Use microSD over SPI for Rev A storage
design_decisions.rationale: microSD makes long field tests and manual audio inspection easy before final storage architecture is chosen.
design_decisions.impact: Firmware must handle card removal, full-card state and write failures.

design_decisions.title: Make mute a physical hardware state
design_decisions.rationale: A wearable recording device must expose an unambiguous privacy control.
design_decisions.impact: Firmware must sample SW_MUTE on boot/wake and must not write audio while muted.

constraints.name: rf_layout
rules: Keep RF trace short and impedance controlled.
Retain pi-network footprints for RF tuning.

constraints.name: crystal_layout
rules: Place 40 MHz crystal close to ESP32-S3.
Keep crystal traces short and away from high-current or switching nodes.

constraints.name: memory_layout
rules: Place flash and PSRAM close to ESP32-S3.
Verify exact ESP32-S3 memory pin mapping before PCB layout.

constraints.name: audio_acoustic_layout
rules: Place MEMS microphone acoustic ports on the outward-facing badge edge.
Keep acoustic ports clear of enclosure ribs, clip hardware, adhesive and fabric blockage.
Keep switching regulator, motor and RF high-current paths away from microphones.

constraints.name: storage_access
rules: Place microSD socket where the card can be accessed during prototype testing.
Add ESD protection if the socket is externally accessible in the final mechanical design.

constraints.name: privacy_control
rules: Physical mute switch state must be readable at boot and wake.
Firmware must block microphone capture and audio file writes while muted.
Recording/privacy LED behavior must not be repurposed for unrelated decorative status.

risks: ESP32-S3 bare-chip symbol pin names are placeholders until exact variant and KiCad symbol are selected.
Flash/PSRAM interface nets must be verified against Espressif reference design before layout.
RF matching values are placeholders and require tuning.
LDO-based 3.3 V rail may not meet all-day efficiency goals.
I2S microphone left/right select polarity and data sharing must be verified after selecting the exact microphone.
microSD socket pinout and card-detect behavior are placeholders until the exact socket is selected.
Mute switch is GPIO-enforced in Rev A; a future revision may need hardware microphone power gating for stronger privacy.
